items.heading: ISCET
items.text: NASTeC is the appliance repair industry's own national certification exam, administered by the nonprofit ISCET. It's voluntary, so it's worth asking whether your technician holds it.

items.icon: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M7 3h7l4 4v14a1 1 0 0 1-1 1H7a1 1 0 0 1-1-1V4a1 1 0 0 1 1-1z"/><path d="M14 3v4h4"/><path d="M9 13h6M9 17h6M9 9h2"/></svg>
items.heading: EPA
items.text: Anyone who services a refrigerator, freezer, or other appliance containing refrigerant is legally required to hold EPA Section 608 certification. See what that actually requires.

items.icon: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 3 2 20h20L12 3z"/><path d="M12 10v3.5"/><path d="M12 16.5h.01"/></svg>
items.heading: CPSC
items.text: Check whether your specific appliance has an open safety recall before paying for a repair — some recalls cover the fix or a replacement for free.

items.icon: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 21a6 6 0 0 0 6-6c0-3-2-5-3-7 0 2-1 3-2 2-1-1-1-3 0-5-3 1-5 4-5 7 0 1 .3 2 1 3-1-.3-2-1-2-2.5A6 6 0 0 0 6 15a6 6 0 0 0 6 6z"/></svg>
items.heading: NFPA
items.text: A poorly repaired dryer, range, or water heater is a real fire risk. The National Fire Protection Association's home safety guidance covers what to check after any appliance service.

items.heading: BBB
items.text: Look up any appliance repair company's complaint history, customer reviews, and accreditation status — a free, independent check before you hire.
